newsitem.title: MEXICO: Alberto Saba to sell stake in TV Azteca in IPO.
newsitem.headline: Alberto Saba to sell stake in TV Azteca in IPO.

text.p: Mexican broadcaster TV Azteca on Thursday said one of its board members, Alberto Saba, would sell a portion of his stake in the firm as part of its initial public offering.
The company, Mexico's second largest media firm, announced a global IPO earlier this week worth between $600-$680 million and expected to take place in a few months.
But Azteca President Ricardo Salinas Pliego said he was not selling any of his controlling interest and the sale would come from minority shareholders.
The company said in a statement that Saba would stay on as a member of the board of directors and that his son Moises would keep his post as executive president, the number two spot.
Analysts said the Sabas together own about 20 percent of the company's stock and were key in helping Salinas Pliego build up the firm following its 1993 privatization.
Mexican newspaper Reforma said in June the Sabas and Salinas Pliego would soon part ways because of disagreements over the company's management, rumors emphatically denied by the company.
On Thursday, a company spokesman told Reuters he had nothing to add to the firm's statement.
